text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I am sorry about your father's death. C contacted me about his house and will. I will help you, B, and C look for a plan, but I cannot make legal decisions or move money.

I will track NCEs, meaning needs, concerns, and expectations. Here is the first shared NCE list. C needs a plan that does not require her to approve a "family discount" she rejects. A may want to buy the house with her husband at a "family discount", and A should confirm or correct that. B may need money from the house, and B should confirm or correct that. All three sisters need clear facts about the will, who is handling the estate, and the house's value. My own NCEs are that I need a fair process. I am concerned that a rushed deal could damage trust. I expect each sister to see and correct the list before we judge any plan.

This list may be wrong. You can reject or change any item, including mine, and I will update it. I will share the list and any draft plan with all three of you, unless someone asks me to keep a detail private.

C said you and your husband want to buy the house at a "family discount". Please tell me what you propose, why that price seems fair, what price or formula you have in mind, what the will says in your own words, who is handling the estate, what you know about the house's value, what deadline or money pressure you face, and what outcome you could accept. Please also tell me where I have the list wrong.

Thank you. I do want to buy the house with my husband, and I would prefer a family discount. I think keeping it within the family could be fair, but I know C may not agree. We have no price or formula in mind yet, and I can’t say what would be acceptable to everyone.

I suggest a process, not a decision. First, each of you should look for a copy of the will and the name of the person handling the estate. Please send me what you find, and I will share it with the others unless you ask me to keep a detail private. Second, all three should receive the same valuation. An independent appraisal and a local market estimate would give one shared starting number. Third, we should learn the costs tied to the house, such as a mortgage, repairs, taxes, and bills. Fourth, each sister can state the smallest outcome she could accept, including cash needs and timing. Fifth, we can compare options against the NCE list. I see a sale to A at full market value, a sale to A at a discount only if all three freely agree in writing, an open-market sale with proceeds split as the will directs, and a payment plan with the amount, dates, and protections written down. Sixth, no one should sign or pay until all three have the facts, time to review, and a written agreement handled through the estate process. Silence will not count as agreement. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. A lawyer may need to act, and the estate representative may need to act.

I have a draft working plan, not a sale. First, all three of you look for the will, any later change to the will, the deed, and the name of the person handling the estate. Please do not enter the house or remove papers alone. Agree on a joint search, or ask the estate representative to handle it. If no representative is known, a lawyer can explain how to find or appoint one. Second, all three receive the same copies of each paper. Third, all three choose one independent appraiser. The appraisal and a local market estimate go to all three. Fourth, all three receive one shared list of estate costs, such as a mortgage, repairs, taxes, bills, and fees. I will not assume equal shares. The will and the estate process must set each share.

Fifth, you and your husband can seek financing advice after you see the valuation. A purchase at full market value may then be possible. If you cannot afford it, no one should lower B's share or C's share to bridge the gap. A discount would need free written agreement from all three, and you and your husband would need to cover the gap from your own funds. You cannot promise that without the amount and your finances. That remains undecided. C has not approved that now. Sixth, if a sale to A is not possible, an open-market sale can be compared. A could match a real outside offer if the estate process allows. Proceeds would be handled as the will directs. Any payment plan would need the amount, dates, and protections written down. Seventh, no one signs or pays until all three have the facts, time to review, and a written agreement handled through the estate process. Silence will not count as agreement. I cannot make legal decisions or move money. A lawyer may need to act, and the estate representative may need to act.
